jobs.title: Technical Director, DataEdge Strategy & Architecture
jobs.description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!

Job Description Summary:

The Technical Director defines and drives the technical strategy across the DataEdge portfolio. In close partnership with Product Management, Engineering, Support, and executive leadership, this role aligns product roadmaps, platform investments, and architectural decisions with customer needs, business objectives, and Rocket’s strategy to become a platform company.

The DataEdge portfolio includes Rocket’s data integration, replication, synchronization, virtualization, and data intelligence solutions. It helps customers unlock enterprise data across distributed, cloud, and mainframe environments by making trusted data available where it is needed. As AI adoption accelerates, DataEdge delivers trusted, connected, and actionable information to the applications, platforms, models, agents, and intelligent business processes that power modern digital enterprises.

This role will evolve the portfolio into an integrated platform through cloud-native architecture, shared services, AI-enabled innovation, and cross-product collaboration. The Technical Director will also work with peer technical leaders to shape the Data Modernization business unit’s technical strategy, identify shared opportunities, and align architecture and investment decisions across portfolios. Success requires technical leadership and the ability to build alignment and shared ownership.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Partner with Product Management to define the DataEdge platform strategy and translate business priorities into a shared, cross-product technical roadmap.
Build alignment across Product, Engineering, and Architecture, balancing product needs with DataEdge platform objectives and the shared technical direction of the Data Modernization business unit.
Work with peer technical leaders to shape the Data Modernization business unit’s technical strategy, align investments, and identify shared platform opportunities.
Drive reusable services, APIs, frameworks, and common platform capabilities while consolidating overlapping technologies.
Define cloud-native strategies for deployment, configuration, scalability, observability, security, and operational excellence.
Partner with Product and Engineering to identify, prioritize, and deliver AI platform capabilities, intelligent automation, MCP, and agentic systems that create measurable customer value and competitive differentiation.
Represent the DataEdge technology vision internally and externally. Use customer input, industry trends, analyst perspectives, emerging technologies, and competitive insight to shape strategy and investment priorities.
Shape DataEdge’s role in the broader data, analytics, and AI ecosystem through technology partnerships, industry standards, open APIs, and interoperability frameworks.
Raise engineering effectiveness across the portfolio by advancing AI-enabled development, testing, documentation, modernization, and delivery practices.
Lead architecture reviews, communicate decisions and tradeoffs, and mentor Principal Engineers, architects, and other senior technical leaders.

Required Qualifications:

12+ years of software engineering, architecture, or technical leadership experience.
Proven experience defining architecture and technology strategy across multiple enterprise products or platforms and contributing to strategy across a broader business or portfolio.
Strong expertise in LLMs, agentic systems, retrieval architectures, enterprise AI integration, responsible AI patterns, and emerging interoperability standards such as MCP.
Demonstrated delivery of AI-enabled product capabilities and adoption of AI-enabled engineering practices.
Deep expertise in cloud-native architecture, containers, Kubernetes, distributed systems, and modern software delivery.
Experience building shared platforms, services, APIs, or reusable frameworks and leading technology consolidation.
Successful partnership with Product Management on strategy, roadmaps, prioritization, and investment decisions.
Demonstrated ability to work with peer senior technical leaders to shape strategy, resolve cross-portfolio tradeoffs, align technical investments, and influence without direct authority.
Demonstrated ability to shape ecosystem strategy across enterprise data, analytics, and AI, including work with customers, technology partners, industry standards, open APIs, and interoperability frameworks.
Exceptional communication and facilitation skills, including with executive leaders, with demonstrated experience mentoring Principal Engineers, architects, and other senior technical leaders.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, IS, or related technical discipline.

Team Overview

The Director of Credit Risk Solutions Consulting leads a team of Solutions Consultants who partner with Sales and clients to uncover critical business issues and align them with TransUnion's solutions. Serving as a critical component of TransUnion's Trusted Advisor strategy, the team combines deep industry and product expertise with consultative engagement to drive product and solutions adoption, strengthen client relationships, and provide market insights that influence product strategy, innovation, and solution development. This is a hybrid position and involves regular performance of job responsibilities virtually as well as in-person at an assigned TU office location for a minimum of two days a week.

Role Overview And Core Responsibilities

This role is responsible for defining and leading the evolution of the Solutions Consulting function, including consulting methodologies, engagement models, capability development, and resource deployment. The successful candidate will establish a scalable operating model that maximizes efficiency, supports strategic growth priorities, and strengthens TransUnion's position as a trusted advisor to customers. Working closely with Sales, Product, Data Science, and other business leaders, this role will drive a more integrated and consultative approach to solution adoption while ensuring the organization maintains a compelling, market-leading point of view. The leader will lead by example through direct engagements for key clients and strategic initiatives, while building, coaching and developing a high-performing team and cultivating future leadership talent.

This role contributes directly to achieving TransUnion's annual revenue and growth objectives by:

Identifying market opportunities and partnering with Sales leadership to influence account strategies, client engagement, and pipeline development.
Establishing compelling customer narratives, business cases, and thought leadership that articulate the value and impact of TransUnion's products and solutions.
Leading continuous improvement of the Solutions Consulting operating model and cross-functional engagement processes to increase effectiveness, scalability, and efficiency.
Ensuring the team maintains a deep understanding of market trends, competitive dynamics, and emerging customer needs, translating insights into actionable recommendations.
This role will partner with Product, Marketing, Data Science, and Sales leadership to develop and align thought leadership that supports customer engagement, market positioning, and solution adoption.
Representing TransUnion externally through industry events, strategic customer engagements, and market-facing initiatives that reinforce the company's Trusted Advisor brand.

Required Knowledge And Experiences

10+ years’ of progressive experience in Consulting, Product Management, Risk Management, Analytics, or Financial Services, including leadership of complex, high impact initiatives
5+ years of experience leading cross-functional teams and influencing stakeholders in a matrixed environment.
Bachelor’s degree in sciences, mathematics, statistics, or related field such as business, finance, economics, or equivalent.
Understanding of Credit Risk fundamentals and how credit lifecycle strategies are developed/managed e.g., using the right set of internal or credit bureau attributes/scores that help drive revenue and reduce losses.
Must have a business understanding of respective product(s) P&L e.g. profitability and loss provisions.
Understanding of credit bureau(s) data is preferred.
Proficient in building PowerPoint presentations with clear messaging.
Advanced Excel skills and proficiency in managing formulas and pivot tables.
Basic SQL and data analysis skills is an asset.
Excellent communication skills (oral & written) with ability to communicate complex concepts and solutions successfully to all levels of management and technical expertise.
Must have proven ability to interact and mediate with all levels of organization, from most junior to most senior, from all aspects of business including technical and operational.

The expected pay range for this position is $174,000 - $245,000 annually. The pay information provided for this position reflects a reasonable estimate of the range of expected compensation for this job. In addition, variable compensation is based on applicable company guidance and plan documents as well as performance.

Assumer la responsabilité de la conception de la solution et des décisions en matière d’architecture et fournir des directives à cet égard, en assurant l’harmonisation avec l’architecture d’entreprise, l’évolutivité et la maintenabilité à long terme.

Our Purpose

At Deloitte, our Purpose is to make an impact that matters. We exist to inspire and help our people, organizations, communities, and countries to thrive by building a better future. Our work underpins a prosperous society where people can find meaning and opportunity. It builds consumer and business confidence, empowers organizations to find imaginative ways of deploying capital, enables fair, trusted, and functioning social and economic institutions, and allows our friends, families, and communities to enjoy the quality of life that comes with a sustainable future. And as the largest 100% Canadian-owned and operated professional services firm in our country, we are proud to work alongside our clients to make a positive impact for all Canadians.

By living our Purpose, we will make an impact that matters.

Have many careers in one Firm.
Enjoy flexible, proactive, and practical benefits that foster a culture of well-being and connectedness.
Learn from deep subject matter experts through mentoring and on the job coaching

--

What will your typical day look like?

As a Director within Deloitte’s Deal Transformation & Post Merger Integration (DT&PMI) Human Resources Due Diligence (HRDD) practice, you will play a leadership role in advising private equity investors and corporate clients on the financial, operational and strategic implications of human capital matters across complex M&A transactions.

Combining strong commercial judgment, quantitative analytical capabilities and human capital expertise, you will lead financially focused due diligence engagements to identify and quantify material transaction risks, assess historical and prospective workforce costs, and uncover opportunities for EBITDA improvement and enterprise value creation.

Your work will span complex compensation and benefits arrangements, pensions and other employee liabilities, workforce cost structures, organizational effectiveness and carve-out considerations. You will translate these findings into actionable insights that inform transaction economics, deal structuring, negotiations and post-acquisition priorities.

Beyond leading engagements, you will serve as a trusted advisor to senior client stakeholders, collaborate with multidisciplinary deal teams, mentor and develop high-performing professionals, and contribute to the continued growth of the practice.

Responsibilities

Lead Transaction Due Diligence: Direct financially focused human capital due diligence engagements, identifying and quantifying material risks, liabilities, cost exposures and opportunities that could influence transaction value, deal terms and post-closing priorities.
Assess Financial and Commercial Deal Implications: Analyze historical and projected workforce costs, including compensation, benefits, pensions, executive arrangements and transaction-related obligations, to evaluate implications for normalized EBITDA, net debt, cash flow and transaction economics.
Drive Value Creation: Identify and assess opportunities for labor cost optimization, workforce productivity, organizational effectiveness, spans and layers improvements, and sustainable EBITDA enhancement.
Lead Workforce Analytics and Financial Modeling: Direct complex quantitative analyses using workforce, payroll and financial datasets, developing robust models and defensible financial estimates despite incomplete or imperfect information.
Advise on Carve-outs and Standalone Requirements: Assess standalone operating models, workforce structures, stranded costs, incremental costs, employee transition requirements and Transition Service Agreements (TSAs).
Deliver Executive-Level Insights: Synthesize complex technical findings into clear, commercially relevant recommendations for private equity investors, corporate executives, investment teams and other transaction stakeholders.
Collaborate Across Deal Disciplines: Work closely with Financial Due Diligence, M&A, tax, legal, operational and technology advisory teams to connect human capital findings to the broader transaction thesis and diligence conclusions.
Lead Client Engagements and Develop Talent: Independently manage complex engagements, facilitate discussions with senior management, oversee delivery quality, and mentor, coach and develop high-performing teams.
Contribute to Practice Growth: Develop trusted client relationships, support business development, identify cross-functional opportunities and help expand Deloitte’s human capital transaction advisory capabilities.

About The Team

Our Human Resources Due Diligence practice is part of Deloitte’s Strategy, Risk & Transactions (SR&T) business, within the Deal Transformation & Post Merger Integration (DT&PMI) team.

We operate at the intersection of M&A, finance and human capital, helping private equity investors and corporate clients understand how workforce-related risks, liabilities, costs and opportunities influence deal value.

Our engagements combine transaction advisory, quantitative analysis and specialized human capital expertise, often in close collaboration with Financial Due Diligence and other M&A advisory teams.

Joining our growing practice offers the opportunity to advise on complex, high-profile transactions, work across diverse industries and jurisdictions, mentor and develop talented professionals, and contribute to building a differentiated advisory offering within Deloitte’s M&A business.

Enough About Us, Let’s Talk About You

Transaction Advisory and Commercial Acumen: Strong understanding of M&A transactions, investment considerations and financial drivers of deal value, with the ability to connect human capital findings to transaction economics and business decisions.
Quantitative and Financial Analytical Capabilities: Ability to interpret complex financial and workforce information, assess cost structures, build or review financial models, and evaluate implications for EBITDA, net debt, cash flow and enterprise value.
Human Capital Expertise: Strong knowledge of workforce costs, compensation, employee benefits, pensions, executive arrangements, organizational structures or other material human capital considerations. Depth in one or more specialized areas and an ability to evaluate broader implications are valued.
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: Exceptional analytical judgment, intellectual curiosity and ability to structure ambiguous problems, challenge assumptions, and derive evidence-based conclusions from incomplete information.
Strategic and Value Creation Orientation: Ability to identify opportunities for organizational effectiveness, operating cost improvement and sustainable value creation, translating findings into actionable recommendations.
Executive Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill complex financial and technical matters into concise, persuasive insights for senior executives, private equity investors and deal stakeholders.
Technical Proficiency: Advanced Excel modeling and PowerPoint skills. Experience with large datasets, payroll or workforce information, or tools such as Power BI, Tableau or SQL is an asset.
Leadership and Talent Development: Ability to lead complex engagements and multidisciplinary teams, mentor professionals, provide constructive feedback, and foster a high-performing team environment.
Client Management: Ability to build trusted relationships with senior clients, manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work under demanding transaction timelines.
Commercial and Growth Mindset: Ability to identify client needs, contribute to business development and help grow a specialized advisory practice.

Minimum Experience

Typically 10+ years of progressive experience in transaction advisory, M&A consulting, human capital advisory, actuarial or rewards consulting, restructuring, operational improvement, or related financial and strategic advisory disciplines, including significant leadership responsibilities.
Experience evaluating complex business issues through quantitative and financial analysis, translating findings into strategic recommendations and measurable commercial outcomes.
Meaningful exposure to M&A transactions, financial due diligence, carve-outs, integrations, business transformation or value creation initiatives. Experience leading human capital due diligence engagements is a strong asset.
Understanding of workforce-related financial and operational considerations, supported by experience in compensation, benefits, pensions, workforce analytics, organizational effectiveness or labor cost optimization.
Proven success leading multidisciplinary engagements, advising senior stakeholders, mentoring professionals and building trusted client relationships.
Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, mathematics, actuarial science, statistics, business, engineering or a related quantitative or analytical discipline.
CFA, CPA, CBV or actuarial designations (e.g., ASA, ACIA, FSA, FCIA), or equivalent qualifications, are assets.

Total Rewards

The salary range for this position is $157,000 - $293,000, and individuals may be eligible to participate in our bonus program. Deloitte is fair and competitive when it comes to the salaries of our people. We regularly benchmark across a variety of positions, industries, sectors, targets, and levels. Our approach is grounded on recognizing people's unique strengths and contributions and rewarding the value that they deliver.

Our Total Rewards Package extends well beyond traditional compensation and benefit programs and is designed to recognize employee contributions, encourage personal wellness, and support firm growth. Along with a competitive base salary and variable pay opportunities, we offer a wide array of initiatives that differentiate us as a people-first organization. On top of our regular paid vacation days, some examples include: $4,000 per year for mental health support benefits, a $1,300 flexible benefit spending account, firm-wide closures known as "Deloitte Days", dedicated days of for learning (known as Development and Innovation Days), flexible work arrangements and a hybrid work structure.

We are a group of talented people who want to learn, gain experience, and develop skills. Wherever you are in your career, we want you to advance.

You Shape How We Make Impact.

Diverse perspectives and life experiences make us better. Whoever you are and wherever you’re from, we want you to feel like you belong here. We provide flexible working options to support you and how you can contribute.

Be the leader you want to be

Some guide teams, some change culture, some build essential expertise. We offer opportunities and experiences that support your continuing growth as a leader.

What will your typical day look like?

As a Director within Deloitte’s Deal Transformation & Post Merger Integration (DT&PMI) Human Resources Due Diligence (HRDD) practice, you will play a leadership role in advising private equity investors and corporate clients on the financial, operational and strategic implications of human capital matters across complex M&A transactions.

Combining strong commercial judgment, quantitative analytical capabilities and human capital expertise, you will lead financially focused due diligence engagements to identify and quantify material transaction risks, assess historical and prospective workforce costs, and uncover opportunities for EBITDA improvement and enterprise value creation.

Your work will span complex compensation and benefits arrangements, pensions and other employee liabilities, workforce cost structures, organizational effectiveness and carve-out considerations. You will translate these findings into actionable insights that inform transaction economics, deal structuring, negotiations and post-acquisition priorities.

Beyond leading engagements, you will serve as a trusted advisor to senior client stakeholders, collaborate with multidisciplinary deal teams, mentor and develop high-performing professionals, and contribute to the continued growth of the practice.

Responsibilities

Lead Transaction Due Diligence: Direct financially focused human capital due diligence engagements, identifying and quantifying material risks, liabilities, cost exposures and opportunities that could influence transaction value, deal terms and post-closing priorities.
Assess Financial and Commercial Deal Implications: Analyze historical and projected workforce costs, including compensation, benefits, pensions, executive arrangements and transaction-related obligations, to evaluate implications for normalized EBITDA, net debt, cash flow and transaction economics.
Drive Value Creation: Identify and assess opportunities for labor cost optimization, workforce productivity, organizational effectiveness, spans and layers improvements, and sustainable EBITDA enhancement.
Lead Workforce Analytics and Financial Modeling: Direct complex quantitative analyses using workforce, payroll and financial datasets, developing robust models and defensible financial estimates despite incomplete or imperfect information.
Advise on Carve-outs and Standalone Requirements: Assess standalone operating models, workforce structures, stranded costs, incremental costs, employee transition requirements and Transition Service Agreements (TSAs).
Deliver Executive-Level Insights: Synthesize complex technical findings into clear, commercially relevant recommendations for private equity investors, corporate executives, investment teams and other transaction stakeholders.
Collaborate Across Deal Disciplines: Work closely with Financial Due Diligence, M&A, tax, legal, operational and technology advisory teams to connect human capital findings to the broader transaction thesis and diligence conclusions.
Lead Client Engagements and Develop Talent: Independently manage complex engagements, facilitate discussions with senior management, oversee delivery quality, and mentor, coach and develop high-performing teams.
Contribute to Practice Growth: Develop trusted client relationships, support business development, identify cross-functional opportunities and help expand Deloitte’s human capital transaction advisory capabilities.

About The Team

Our Human Resources Due Diligence practice is part of Deloitte’s Strategy, Risk & Transactions (SR&T) business, within the Deal Transformation & Post Merger Integration (DT&PMI) team.

We operate at the intersection of M&A, finance and human capital, helping private equity investors and corporate clients understand how workforce-related risks, liabilities, costs and opportunities influence deal value.

Our engagements combine transaction advisory, quantitative analysis and specialized human capital expertise, often in close collaboration with Financial Due Diligence and other M&A advisory teams.

Joining our growing practice offers the opportunity to advise on complex, high-profile transactions, work across diverse industries and jurisdictions, mentor and develop talented professionals, and contribute to building a differentiated advisory offering within Deloitte’s M&A business.

Enough About Us, Let’s Talk About You

Transaction Advisory and Commercial Acumen: Strong understanding of M&A transactions, investment considerations and financial drivers of deal value, with the ability to connect human capital findings to transaction economics and business decisions.
Quantitative and Financial Analytical Capabilities: Ability to interpret complex financial and workforce information, assess cost structures, build or review financial models, and evaluate implications for EBITDA, net debt, cash flow and enterprise value.
Human Capital Expertise: Strong knowledge of workforce costs, compensation, employee benefits, pensions, executive arrangements, organizational structures or other material human capital considerations. Depth in one or more specialized areas and an ability to evaluate broader implications are valued.
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: Exceptional analytical judgment, intellectual curiosity and ability to structure ambiguous problems, challenge assumptions, and derive evidence-based conclusions from incomplete information.
Strategic and Value Creation Orientation: Ability to identify opportunities for organizational effectiveness, operating cost improvement and sustainable value creation, translating findings into actionable recommendations.
Executive Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill complex financial and technical matters into concise, persuasive insights for senior executives, private equity investors and deal stakeholders.
Technical Proficiency: Advanced Excel modeling and PowerPoint skills. Experience with large datasets, payroll or workforce information, or tools such as Power BI, Tableau or SQL is an asset.
Leadership and Talent Development: Ability to lead complex engagements and multidisciplinary teams, mentor professionals, provide constructive feedback, and foster a high-performing team environment.
Client Management: Ability to build trusted relationships with senior clients, manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work under demanding transaction timelines.
Commercial and Growth Mindset: Ability to identify client needs, contribute to business development and help grow a specialized advisory practice.

Experience evaluating complex business issues through quantitative and financial analysis, translating findings into strategic recommendations and measurable commercial outcomes.

Understanding of workforce-related financial and operational considerations, supported by experience in compensation, benefits, pensions, workforce analytics, organizational effectiveness or labor cost optimization.
Proven success leading multidisciplinary engagements, advising senior stakeholders, mentoring professionals and building trusted client relationships.

CFA, CPA, CBV or actuarial designations (e.g., ASA, ACIA, FSA, FCIA), or equivalent qualifications, are assets.

liase with exploration management, KTS, and site geology teams to ensure database structures support geological, resource, and reserve modelling requirements.

Own forecasting and pipeline management. You’ll own the forecasting process and cadence, delivering accurate, defensible revenue forecasts across new business, renewals, and expansion for a business built on annually re-sold media programs. You’ll establish pipeline hygiene standards, stage definitions, and inspection rhythms; run weekly pipeline and forecast reviews with Sales leadership; and partner with Finance on bookings-to-revenue reconciliation, campaign delivery pacing, and quarterly business reviews.
Turn commercial data into actionable insights. You’ll build and maintain the reporting suite for the business, including pipeline, win/loss, retention and renewal rates, upsell, rep productivity, and brand- and agency-level performance. You’ll deliver insights that shape strategy — identifying where we’re winning, where deals stall, and which therapeutic areas and agency relationships are growing — and present those insights to senior leadership. You’ll also define and govern a single source of truth for commercial data across systems.
Scale systems, tools, and AI capabilities. You’ll own the sales technology stack — with Salesforce as the backbone, alongside forecasting, enablement, data enrichment, and workflow tools — including administration, roadmap, integrations, and vendor management. Improve deal support and commercial processes. You’ll continuously identify and remove friction across the quote-to-cash process and own rules of engagement across Sales, Client Experience, and Market Development.
Scale sales best practices. You’ll identify what’s working across outreach cadences, deal motions, and renewal plays and scale those practices across the team to shorten sales cycles and maximize selling time. You’ll partner closely with Sales Enablement and Training, which is owned separately, to ensure process changes, tooling, and best practices are embedded in onboarding and ongoing coaching.
Lead and develop the Sales Operations team. You’ll lead, develop, and mentor an established Sales Operations team spanning analytics, systems administration, and deal support, shaping the function’s structure as the business grows. Have demonstrated ownership of forecasting, territory and quota planning, and sales compensation design within a quota-carrying sales organization

Building on a long legacy of innovation and technical excellence, we continue to evolve our capabilities to address modern and emerging risks—from cyber and artificial intelligence to connected technologies.

Primary Objectives

The Director, Systems & Data Transformation is accountable for shaping and executing HSB Canada’s enterprise systems, data, and digital transformation agenda. Acting as a strategic partner to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, the Director translates business priorities into an integrated multi-year roadmap, leads complex cross-functional programs, and delivers measurable improvements in growth, customer and broker experience, operational effectiveness, decision-making, and risk management.

The role provides strategic and operational leadership for the transformation and optimization of the Guidewire ecosystem and its surrounding applications, integrations, data platforms, and controls, ensuring reliable and scalable support for policy, billing, claims, underwriting, and insurance operations.

The Director also leads the delivery of major business-facing capabilities, including Quote, Bind and Issue (QBI), underwriting workflow, digital experiences, enterprise data products, analytics, and responsible AI solutions, in close partnership with business, technology, operations, risk, and global stakeholders.

Success requires an enterprise-minded leader who can connect strategy, architecture, data, delivery, change management, and operational execution; build high-performing multidisciplinary teams; and establish the governance, partnerships, and performance disciplines needed to sustain transformation outcomes.

Job Responsibilities

Transformation Strategy & Portfolio Delivery
Define and maintain an integrated, multi-year systems, data, and digital transformation strategy aligned with enterprise priorities and target business outcomes
Own the transformation portfolio from business case and prioritization through delivery, adoption, value realization, and transition to operations
Establish portfolio governance, roadmaps, investment plans, budgets, resource capacity, milestones, benefits, and executive reporting
Manage cross-program dependencies, delivery risks, organizational constraints, and competing priorities; escalate decisions with clear options and recommendations
Define measurable outcomes and key performance indicators, using performance insights to continuously improve delivery and business value
Core Systems Transformation & Guidewire Leadership

Lead major core-platform initiatives, including ClaimCenter transformation, while maintaining service continuity, production stability, support readiness, and effective control design

Data Science & Responsible AI

Ensure data and AI solutions are explainable, secure, measurable, and embedded into business processes and decisions

Geotab ® is a global leader in IoT and connected transportation and certified “Great Place to Work™.” We are a company of diverse and talented individuals who work together to help businesses grow and succeed, and increase the safety and sustainability of our communities.

Processing billions of data points a day, Geotab leverages data analytics and machine learning to improve productivity, optimize fleets through the reduction of fuel consumption, enhance driver safety and achieve strong compliance to regulatory changes.
Our team is growing and we’re looking for people who follow their passion, think differently and want to make an impact. Ours is a fast paced, ever changing environment. Geotabbers accept that challenge and are willing to take on new tasks and activities - ones that may not always be described in the initial job description. Join us for a fulfilling career with opportunities to innovate, great benefits, and our fun and inclusive work culture. Reach your full potential with Geotab. Who You Are

We are always looking for amazing talent who can contribute to our growth and deliver results ! Geotab is seeking a Head of Security Centre who will own Geotab's vehicle and asset security outcome end to end — theft prevention (Starter Inhibit, immobilization and relay-kit solutions), stolen-asset tracking, and recovery — with successful recovery rate as the domain's primary KPA . If you love technology, and are keen to join an industry leader — we would love to hear from you !

What You'll Do

As a Head of Security Centre, your key area of responsibility will be owning the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for the Security Centre, operating as a hands-on product owner and business owner to translate strategic direction into a validated business case and roadmap . You will need to work closely with Asset Tracking, Lost Mode and security operations centre integrations, Shared Mobility, Embedded Engineering, and Platform domains .
To be successful in this role you will be a self-starter energized by owning a domain single-handedly, with a Geotab First mindset, strong communication skills, and the ability to build effective cross-functional partnerships . In addition, the successful candidate will have deep customer empathy, commercial instinct with P&L literacy, and AI nativity to redesign workflows and compress effort

Own the overarching product vision, strategy, and roadmap for the Security Centre while taking full accountability for key business outcomes like vehicle recovery rates .
Personally drive end-to-end product discovery, requirements, prioritization, and delivery while leveraging AI tools to optimize single-person domain reach .
Validate new business cases by sizing the market, mapping key competitors, and testing willingness to pay across target markets before scaling .
Manage and maintain existing theft-prevention offerings—including Starter Inhibit, immobilization, and relay-kit solutions—to ensure continuous product health and ownership .
Establish direct feedback loops with external fleet customers, sales, and support teams to identify gaps and continuously refine product features .
Define and track core customer experience and business performance metrics, including adoption, retention, time-to-value, NPS, and overall domain revenue .
Collaborate with platform, segment, and solution domain leads—such as Asset Tracking and Shared Mobility—to deliver a seamless theft-prevention-to-recovery user journey .
Present data-driven growth recommendations, commercial investment cases, and annual budget input directly to department board leadership .
Advocate for a "Geotab First" collaborative mindset by building strong cross-functional partnerships and prioritizing company-wide goals over domain silos

10 - 12 years of required previous experience in related fields .
7+ years of experience in product management, product engineering, or a related customer-facing product role, ideally in telematics, vehicle security, or IoT .
3+ years owning a product line or business outcome end to end, including building and validating business cases .
5 - 8 years of required leadership experience, including 2+ years in a role with accountability for customer-facing outcomes and cross-functional coordination (demonstrated ability to lead through influence across multiple teams and domains) .
Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience) .
Domain knowledge of vehicle security and anti-theft (immobilization, starter inhibit, keyless access, jamming/spoofing) with deep customer empathy and P&L literacy .
AI Nativity to redesign domain workflows around AI, a self-starter mindset to own a single-person domain hands-on, and the ability to travel routinely (approx. 10–15%) .
